The above subscriptions totalling
$1,210.00 were made as the outcome of a notice issued
by the General Labour Union on October 7, 1933,
requesting local labour unions to financially assist
the strikers in question.

The funds thus collected, with the
exception of $300.00, have been used to defray the
expenses of press notices, strike propaganda, the
support of picket groups and the general operation of the
Union offices. Unexpended monies have been
placed in the custody of Wi Wen-foo (何文高), Chu
Hao-sung (朱浩森) and Yang Shao-keng (楊肇),
members of the Strike Committee of the 4th District
Water & Electricity Workers' Union.

In addition to the foregoing, Chu
Hsueh-fan and Loh Ching-dz, who are "dukees" of Tu
Yueh-sung, and Chu Hao-sung, member of the Strike Committee
of the 4th District Water & Electricity Workers'
Union, succeeded at the beginning of November, 1933,
in obtaining a loan of $10,000.00 from Tu Yueh-sung,
in the name of the General Labour Union and the 4th District
Water & Electricity Workers' Union. A sum of
$6,000.00 has been paid over by Tu to the three labour
agitators referred to above, who in conjunction with
Yih Ziang-kao (葉翔皋), committee member of the
Shipwrights' Union, and Pao Tuh-foh (包德福) and
Yang Shao-keng (楊肇賡), members of the Strike
Committee of the 4th District Water & Electricity

Date. November 22, 1935.

Subject (in full) Shanghai Power Company.

Made by D. S. I. Golder Forwarded by Whouman ASD

Information obtained by Agent 59
The General Labour Union and the 4th District Water & Electricity Workers' Union convened a meeting of representatives of the workers of the Shanghai Power Company at 3 p.m. November 21 in the offices of the General Labour Union, 117 Foh Yeu Road, City. Some 200 persons including the 56 dismissed hands, attended.
On arriving at the General Labour Union, the 56 dismissed workers together with some ten other strikers, under the leadership of Yang Keng-sung (杨根松), expressed their opposition to the terms ~~of the terms~~ of the settlement and vilified the representatives of the strikers who had accepted the dismissal of the 56 workers. They demanded the presence of Chu Hsueh-fan (朱学范), committee member of the General Labour Union, to explain why these terms should be accepted without the consent of the workers. They further declared that the workers, who handled the settlement of the trouble, were not representatives of the strikers and that the workers would not acknowledge the settlement. Yih Ziang-káó (叶翔皋), committee member of the General Labour Union, who received the malcontents, was surrounded and threatened by them but eventually persuaded them to listen to the terms of settlement. Yih and Loong Pei-yuin (龙佩玉), another committee member of the General Labour Union, in speech stated that Tu settled the strike for the welfare of the public as well as the workers and that a 5% superannuation gratuity would be issued to the dismissed workers.

（左侧手写批注：Shi 20/11）

特工59获取的情报
总工会和第四区水电职工工会于11月21日下午3时在市内北四川路117号总工会办事处召开了上海电力公司工人代表会议。包括被解雇的56名工人在内的约200人出席了会议。
抵达总工会后，这56名被解雇的工人在杨根松（Yang Keng-sung）的带领下，连同其他十余名罢工者，表示反对和解条款，并辱骂那些接受解雇56名工人决定的罢工代表。他们要求总工会委员朱学范（Chu Hsueh-fan）到场，解释为何在未征得工人同意的情况下接受这些条款。他们还声明，处理此次纠纷和解事宜的工人并非罢工者的代表，工人们不会承认该和解协议。接待不满工人的总工会委员叶翔皋（Yih Ziang-káó）被他们包围并受到威胁，但最终说服他们听取和解条款。叶翔皋和另一位总工会委员龙佩玉（Loong Pei-yuin）在发言中表示，杜月笙是为了公众和工人的福利而解决此次罢工的，并将向被解雇的工人发放5%的退休金酬金。

（左侧手写批注：施 20/11）

The meeting was presided over by Sung Tung-sung ( 孙栋生 ), a worker of the Shanghai Power Company, who reported that the following terms were made between Tu Yueh-sung and the Company for the settlement of the strike :-

1. That the workers resume work without delay.
2. That on resumption of work, each striker would be issued with a loan of one month's wages from the Company, for the refunding of which Tu Yueh-sung would be responsible.
3. That 56 workers be dismissed on the payment of a 5% superannuation gratuity.

The following decisions were then reached at the meeting:
1. That the workers be notified to resume work on the morning of November 22.
2. That the dismissed workers should submit their names together with particulars of their services, with the Shanghai Power Company to the General Labour Union or the 4th District Water & Electricity Workers' Union so that the amount of the gratuity to be paid to each man could be calculated.

The meeting terminated at 4.45 p.m.

会议由上海电力公司工人孙栋生（Sung Tung-sung）主持，他报告了杜月笙与公司之间为解决罢工达成的以下条款：-

1. 工人立即复工。
2. 复工时，公司将向每位罢工者提供相当于一个月工资的贷款，由杜月笙负责偿还。
3. 解雇56名工人，并支付5%的退休金酬金。

随后会议达成以下决定：
1. 通知工人于11月22日上午复工。
2. 被解雇的工人应将其姓名及服务详情提交给总工会或第四区水电职工工会，以便计算每人应得的酬金金额，并提交给上海电力公司。

会议于下午4时45分结束。

Information obtained by Agent No.56.
At 1.30 p.m. November 19, Tu Yueh-sung entertained representatives of the Chinese members of the S.M.C., the General Labour Union and the strikers of the Shanghai Power Company to tiffin in the Chinese Bankers' Association, No.4 Hongkong Road. In addressing the 13 persons present, Tu Yueh-sung, who presided, stated that the strike had to be settled as soon as possible so as not to interfere with the routine, business and otherwise, of the local public.
In connection with the offer of the management of the Shanghai Power Company to advance the equivalent of one month's pay to each worker on resumption, to be paid back at the rate of 10% per month, it was decided that Chinese members of the S.M.C. enter into negotiations with the Company with a view to obtaining the sum in question as a gratuity in lieu of pay lost whilst on strike. It was also decided that should the negotiations fail, the total sum advanced to the workers should be subscribed by the mediators.
As to the Company's statement regarding the sixty men whose services are to be terminated, it was concluded that these men should be permitted to resign and that all pay and gratuities due them in such case be paid to them.
The function terminated at 2.30 p.m.

Subject (in full) Shanghai Power Company - Negotiations re Settlement.

Made by D. S. I. Golder Forwarded by W Duncan D.J.S.

During the meeting held in Mr. Messenden's
office on the morning of November 16, Doo Yueh-sung asked
Mr. Hopkins whether the management would pay a gratuity
to the 60 men whose services they have decided to dispense
with. Doo was informed that the actions of the men
in question were looked upon as misconduct and under
such circumstances the men would only receive the
wages due to them up until the date of the commencement
of the strike.

Doo in a roundabout fashion then informed
those present that he had already gone to considerable
expense ($6,000.00) in connection with the matter and
that unless the sixty men were given a small cash payment
when their services were terminated, it might well cause
the present negotiations to break down. Mr. Hopkins
in reply stated that he did not intend to buy the men
off, further that their action in calling a strike was
most unreasonable and was looked upon by conservative
citizens, who were in possession of the full facts of the
case, as totally unjustified.

In connection with the foregoing matter an
interview was obtained to-day with Mr. Heald, General
Manager of the Shanghai Power Company. He stated that
the Company had definitely decided not to pay the sixty
men in question a cent more than they were entitled to
in wages.

Between 9.30 a.m. and 10.30 a.m. November 17,
about 100 strikers held a meeting in the offices of the
4th District Water & Electricity Workers' Union, No. 15

stated that they would have to resume unconditionally

committee had not kept the strikers posted as to the
march of events, thus they were carrying on without any
idea as to how they stood.    Such sentiments were
immediately denounced by others present who insisted that
the Strike Committee be left to handle the affair.    It
was finally decided to send a delegation of four to call
on Doo Yueh-sung to request him to renew his efforts in
bringing about a settlement; it was also decided that

situation.

for the settlement of the Shanghai Power Company labour
dispute as outlined to Doo Yueh-sung during the meeting
held in Mr. Fessenden's office on November 15, show

under which the one month's pay should be advanced.

make fleeting references to the conditions of the
settlement (Vide Intelligence Report of 16/11/33).

At 11.15 a.m. October 6, three representatives of
the General Labour Union, 117 Foh Yeu Road, City, called at
the Municipality of Greater Shanghai and requested that the
organ devise effective measures to bring to an end the
present strike in the Shanghai Power Company. They were
received by O.K. Yui, Secretary to the Municipality, who
informed them that the matter in question is being
investigated. He also instructed the callers to observe
peace and order.

10 月 6 日上午 11:15，三名来自市内福州路 117 号总工会的代表前往大上海市政府，请求该机构制定有效措施以结束上海电力公司目前的罢工。他们受到市政府秘书余介清（O.K. Yui，音译）的接见，余告知他们正在调查此事。他还指示来访者遵守和平与秩序。

Extract from Special Branch S. I. Report
(D.S.I. Golder) on Oct. 10, 1933.

At about 5 p.m. October 9 Chu Hsueh-fan (朱学范),
committee member of the General Labour Union called on Hsu
Sing-loh (徐星六), General Manager of the National Commercial
Bank, No.78 Peking Road and requested him to mediate in the
dispute under report, on behalf of the workers. When
questioned as to the grounds for the request Chu Hsueh-fan
stated that the time had come for the matter to be settled
and that the workers were willing to resume on condition
that the following grants were made:-
(1) That all employees should be paid three months wages
should they leave the company after one year's service.
(2) That the five percent retiring gratuity to all workers
leaving the Company's employ be paid.
(3) That written regulations be posted in the various workshops
so that the workers may know the conditions under which
they are employed.
(4) That the four men dismissed in June and the 3 let out in
September be reinstated.
(5) That full pay be issued to all workers for the period of
the strike.
Mr. Hsu Sing-loh informed the caller that he had already been
in touch with the Company on the subject of settlement and
was of the opinion that the demands made by the workers
would not be met. He then telephoned to Mr. Hopkins,
President of the Shanghai Power Company and asked his opinion
on the matter of mediation. Mr. Hopkins stated that he was
quite prepared to listen to any reasonable suggestion for
the settlement of the dispute but would only accept
representatives of the workers as the mediators. The Company
throughout have evinced their disapproval of the interference
of outsiders in the affairs of the Company, Mr. Hopkins stated
however, so far as he or the Company were concerned there was

（副巡官 Golder）1933 年 10 月 10 日。

10 月 9 日下午 5 时许，总工会委员朱学范拜访了位于北京路 78 号的中国商业银行总经理徐星六（Hsu Sing-loh），请求他代表工人调解上述纠纷。当被问及提出此请求的理由时，朱学范表示，现在是解决此事的时候了，如果满足以下要求，工人们愿意复工：-
(1) 所有员工在公司服务满一年后离职，应支付三个月工资。
(2) 向所有离开公司的工人支付百分之五的退休金。
(3) 在各车间张贴书面规章，以便工人了解其受雇条件。
(4) 恢复六月被解雇的四人和九月被解雇的三人的职务。
(5) 向所有工人发放罢工期间的全额工资。
徐星六先生告知来访者，他已就和解事宜与公司取得联系，并认为工人的要求不会得到满足。随后他致电上海电力公司总经理霍普金斯先生，征求他对调解事宜的意见。霍普金斯先生表示，他完全愿意听取任何合理的解决纠纷建议，但只接受工人代表作为调解人。霍普金斯先生表示，公司一直对外界干涉公司事务表示不满，然而，就他或公司而言，没有

Special Branch,
October 13, 1933.

SECRET

Commissioner of Police.

Sir,

On October 8, I sent for Bang Koong Che
(彭公哲), Political Agent in Shanghai of the
Central Kuomintang Headquarters at Nanking, and told
him that it was my belief that the communists would be
likely to take advantage of the strike in the Shanghai
Power Co., which is a key industry, to increase their
strength in local labour circles, and added that it
was consequently desirable that the dispute be settled
as soon as possible.

As a result of this conversation, Loh Ching
Tze (陸京士) came to see me a couple of days later,
and stated that he believed that the strike in the
Shanghai Power Co. might be solved on the following
conditions:-

1) That five per cent of the amount of wages
earned by a workman during the period of his
service be issued by the Company as retirement
gratuity if the Company wish to dispense with
his service.

2) That pension or compassionate grant be
issued to three dismissed workmen if the Company
refuse to reinstate them.

3) That the wages of workmen during the
period of the strike be issued.

4) That the Company promulgate a set of
regulations governing the employment of
workmen, their dismissal, the giving of warnings,
the imposition of fines, etc.

I took a paper containing these conditions
to Mr. Heald of the Shanghai Power Co. who said that

特别分部，
1933年10月13日。

机密

致警务总监。

先生：

10月8日，我传召了南京国民党中央总部驻沪政治代理人彭公哲（Bang Koong Che），并告诉他，我认为共产党人可能会利用上海电力公司这一关键行业的罢工来增强其在本地劳工界的力量，并补充说，因此最好尽快解决此次纠纷。

谈话之后，陆京士（Loh Ching Tze）于几天后来见我，并表示他认为上海电力公司的罢工可以在以下条件下得到解决：-

1) 如果公司希望解雇工人，应按该工人在职期间所获工资总额的百分之五，由公司发放退休金。

2) 如果公司拒绝复职三名被解雇的工人，则应向这三人发放养老金或抚恤金。

3) 应发放工人在罢工期间的工资。

4) 公司应颁布一套关于雇佣工人、解雇、给予警告、处以罚款等的规章制度。

我将载有这些条件的文件交给上海电力公司的希尔德（Heald）先生，他说

pages.en:
SECRET
-2-
he could not see his way to agree to any of them,
except the last.
On October 12, Loh Ching Tze ( 陸京士 )
sent me through Superintendent Tan the following
revised set of conditions which, he said, might be
used as a basis for negotiations.-

Five per cent is to be deducted monthly from
the wages of the Chinese employees ( staff employees
and workers). This money plus an additional five
per cent set aside by the management should be
deposited with the Company. The deposits should
bear interest and be known as a superannuation
fund. The whole of the fund to which he is
entitled will be issued to an employee whose
services are dispensed with or who is dismissed.
Any worker who commits a crime and is convicted
by the Judicial Authorities will only be entitled
to his rateable monthly deductions.

Addendum. Should the above method be approved of
and be put into execution, the following sums
should be added to the newly introduced
superannuation fund and be given to the employee
at the time of his leaving the Company's service:-

A sum equivalent to 3% of the total wages
which a worker has received since joining
the Company in the event of a worker
having been in the Company's service for
more than a year and less than five years.

A sum equivalent to 4% of the total wages
which a worker has received since joining
the Company in the event of a worker
having been in the Company's service for
more than five years and less than ten
years.

A sum equivalent to 5% of the total wages
which a worker has received since joining
the Company in the event of a worker having
been in the Company's service for more
than ten years.

I took these to Mr. Heald on the afternoon of
October 12 when he stated that the Company would insist
on the employees returning to work unconditionally.
He added that he believed that the employees, with the
exception of a small number, had joined the strike
through intimidation. He added that he would see that
the majority did not suffer in any way as a result of
the dispute, but that he may decline entirely to take
pages.zh:
机密
-2-
他看不出有任何理由同意其中任何条件，除了最后一条。
10月12日，陆京士（陸京士）通过谭巡官向我转交了以下修订后的条件，他说这些条件可用作谈判的基础：-

每月从中国雇员（职员和工人）的工资中扣除百分之五。这笔钱加上管理层另行拨出的百分之五，应存入公司。存款应计息，并称为养老基金。雇员被解雇或辞退时，应向其发放其有权获得的全部基金。任何犯罪并被司法机关定罪的工人，仅有权获得其按比例计算的每月扣款部分。

附注。如果上述方法获得批准并付诸实施，下列款项应加入新设立的养老基金，并在雇员离开公司服务时发给该雇员：-

若工人在公司服务超过一年但不足五年，则发给相当于该工人自加入公司以来所获工资总额3%的款项。

若工人在公司服务超过五年但不足十年，则发给相当于该工人自加入公司以来所获工资总额4%的款项。

若工人在公司服务超过十年，则发给相当于该工人自加入公司以来所获工资总额5%的款项。

10月12日下午，我将这些条件带给希尔德先生，他表示公司将坚持要求雇员无条件复工。他补充说，他认为除少数人外，其他雇员都是因受到恐吓而参加罢工的。他还表示，他将确保大多数人不会因这场纠纷而遭受任何损失，但他可能会完全拒绝录用

In connection with the Shanghai Power Company
labour dispute, the following news item (translation
attached) appeared in the October 25th Issue of the
Central China Daily News and other vernacular newspapers:
"At the request of various public bodies, the
"Shanghai Municipal Council has undertaken the
"mediation. At 3 p.m. yesterday, Mr. Fessenden,
"Secretary General of the Council, invited
"Mr. Doo Yueh-sung, member of the Council of
"the Chinese Municipality, to discuss ways and
"means to settle the trouble".
Efforts have been made to verify this report
from outside sources without success.

关于上海电力公司劳资纠纷，10月25日的《华中日报》及其他白话报纸上刊登了如下新闻（附译文）：
“应各公共团体的请求，
“上海公共租界工部局已承担
“调解工作。昨日下午3时，工部局
“总办费森登（Fessenden）先生邀请

已尝试从外部来源核实此报道，但未成功。

pages.en:
Extract from Special Branch S. 1. Report
(D.S.I. Golder) on Oct. 26. 1933.

Reference my report dated October 25 relative to
the alleged invitation of Doo Yueh-sung (杜月笙) to
mediate in the Shanghai Power Company dispute. Enquiries
show that Doo Yueh -sung attended the office of Mr. Fessenden
during the afternoon of October 24 at the request of Chu
Hsueh-fah (朱学范), who in approaching "Doo" stated that he
represented the strikers of the Shanghai Power Company.
Doo Yueh-sung during his conversation with Mr. Fessenden,
which was interpreted by Tsai Foh Dong (蔡福棠), confidential
employee of the legal firm of Fessenden and Halcomb, stated
that his effort to settle the trouble had been prompted by
his desire to maintain peace and order. No conclusion was
arrived at on October 24 but "Doo" called on Mr. Fessenden
again yesterday when he was requested to prepare terms of
settlement. Since Doo Yueh-sung's name has been connected
with enquiry it is of interest to note that "Doo" is
reported to have approached the management some days ago
with an offer to settle the existing dispute.
pages.zh:
特别分部 S. 1. 报告摘录
（副督察 Golder）1933年10月26日。

参照我10月25日关于据称邀请杜月笙（Doo Yueh-sung）调解上海电力公司纠纷的报告。查询显示，10月24日下午，杜月笙应朱学范（Chu Hsueh-fah）的请求前往费森登先生的办公室，朱学范在接触“杜”时表示他代表上海电力公司的罢工者。杜月笙在与费森登先生的交谈中（由费森登与哈尔科姆律师事务所的保密雇员蔡福棠（Tsai Foh Dong）担任翻译），表示他努力解决此事是出于维护和平与秩序的愿望。10月24日未达成任何结论，但“杜”昨天再次拜访费森登先生，当时他被要求拟定和解条款。鉴于杜月笙的名字与此事调查有关，值得注意的是，据报道，“杜”几天前曾向管理层提出解决现有纠纷的建议。

Shanghai Power Company - Situation

Doo Yueh-sung, member of the Control Committee of
the Chinese Chamber of Commerce and also President of
the French Concession Chinese Ratepayers' Association,
held a meeting at his home at 216 Rue Wagner on October 26,
inviting Loh Ching-dz, member of the Executive Committee
of the local Tangpu, and Chu Hsueh-fan, member of the
General Labour Union, to discuss the Shanghai Power
Company Strike Situation, and any possible means to
settle the dispute. The situation was described
clearly to Mr. Doo Yueh-sung at this meeting.

------

Mr. Li Cheng Tso, representing the Central Tangpu,
arrived in Shanghai on October 26 to try to find a means
of solving the problem of settling the Shanghai Power
Company strike. He went straight to the local
offices of the Kuomintang and to the Bureau of Social
Affairs, to obtain details of the strike situation.
At 2 p.m. he summoned Zee Hung-sung and Nyi Wen-foo,
representatives of the Shanghai Power Company Workers(
General Labour Union, to get their views on the matter.

-------

Mr. Pan Hwa-kuo, Chief of the Workers' Section
of the Ministry of Industry, left for Nanking at 11 p.m.
October 26 after he had completed his enquiries into the
Shanghai Power Company strike situation.

上海电力公司 - 局势

杜月笙，中国商会监理委员会成员，兼法租界华人纳税会会长，于10月26日在其位于瓦格纳路216号的寓所举行会议，邀请当地党部执行委员陆京士（Loh Ching-dz）和总工会会员朱学范（Chu Hsueh-fan），讨论上海电力公司罢工局势及解决纠纷的可能途径。在此次会议上，向杜月笙先生清楚地描述了局势。

------

代表中央党部的李成佐（Li Cheng Tso）先生于10月26日抵达上海，试图寻找解决上海电力公司罢工问题的办法。他直接前往国民党地方办事处和社会局，以获取罢工局势的详细情况。下午2时，他传唤上海电力公司工人（总工会）代表恽鸿松（Zee Hung-sung）和倪文甫（Nyi Wen-foo），听取他们对此事的意见。

-------

实业部劳工司司长潘华国（Pan Hwa-kuo）先生在完成对上海电力公司罢工局势的调查后，于10月26日晚11时前往南京。

Extract from Special Branch S. 1. Report
(D.S.I. Golder) on Oct. 27. 1933.

It is learned that three Chinese, Yuan Li Teng
(袁履登), Chinese member of the S.M.C., Yu Ya Ching
(虞洽卿), also a member of the S.M.C. and another
who was not named visited Mr. A.D. Bell in the Council
Chambers on October 25 and offered their services in the
settlement of the Shanghai Power Company labour dispute.

The Company decided on October 26 to issue
letters, through the Foreigners in charge of departments
to the senior Chinese employees and workers, now on strike,
requesting them to call at the homes of the said Foreigners
where they will receive certain important information.
The information to be given them will be to the effect that
the Company although realising that 70% or 80% of the
workmen do not want to continue the strike, they (the Company)
will not be able to keep their jobs open for an indefinite
period. The scheme is not as it would appear an effort
on the part of the management to unburden themselves of their
obligations to their employees. The senior employees
backed by a large percentage of the workers now on strike
have approached the management indirectly asking that they
be called back to work.

It is the intention of the workers who wish
to resume work to explain to the Union that the strike
having produced no beneficial result and they having wives
and families to support it is their intention to resume
since the management has informed them that their jobs will
be filled in the near future.
pages.zh:
特别分部 S. 1. 报告摘录
（副督察 Golder）1933年10月27日。

获悉，10月25日，三名华人，即工部局华董袁履登（Yuan Li Teng）、同为工部局华董的虞洽卿（Yu Ya Ching）以及另一位未具名人士，在工部局会议室拜访了贝尔（A.D. Bell）先生，并表示愿意协助解决上海电力公司劳资纠纷。

公司于10月26日决定，通过各部门外籍负责人向目前罢工的高级华籍雇员和工人发出信件，请他们到这些外籍负责人的家中，他们将在那里接收某些重要信息。向他们传达的信息大意是，虽然公司认识到70%或80%的工人不希望继续罢工，但公司无法无限期地保留他们的职位。这一计划并非如表面看来是管理层试图摆脱对雇员的义务。目前罢工的大部分工人支持高级雇员，他们已间接接触管理层，要求被召回工作。

希望复工的工人打算向工会解释，由于罢工未产生有益结果，且他们有妻儿需要供养，既然管理层已通知他们其职位将在不久的将来被填补，他们打算复工。

In connection with the offer of Mr. Yueh Li
Teng (袁履登), Mr. Yu Yah-ching (虞洽卿) and Mr. Hsu

关于袁履登（Yueh Li Teng）先生、虞洽卿（Yu Yah-ching）先生和徐星六（Hsu Sing-loh）先生提议调解上海电力公司劳资纠纷一事。贝尔（A.D. Bell）先生于10月27日致信给他们，感谢他们的好意提议，但声明公司无法接受来自外部的调解。

At 10 a.m. October 28, one Li Zun-tso (李人俊),
member of the People's Movement Committee of the Central
Kuomintang arrived at Shanghai from Nanking. He proceeded
to the Municipality of Greater Shanghai and discussed
measures with Mr. O.K. Yu for a settlement of the labour
dispute in the Power Company. It is learned that Li
Zung-tso is of the opinion that the strikers should be
advised to resume work pending negotiation with the Company.

10月28日上午10时，国民党中央民众运动委员会委员李人俊（Li Zun-tso）从南京抵达上海。他前往大上海市政府，与俞鸿钧（O.K. Yu）先生讨论解决电力公司劳资纠纷的措施。据悉，李人俊认为应劝告罢工者在与公司谈判期间先复工。

Extract from Special Branch S. l. Report
(D.S.I. Golder) on Nov. 4, 1933.

Hsu Shing-loh, Ge eral Manager of the National
Commercial Bank, L.T. Yuen, Chinese advisor to the S.M.C.
and Wong Shafo-lai, Chairman of the Chamber of Commerce,
together with numerous other prominent Chinese have formed
a committee and have approached the management of the
Shanghai Power Company with regard to an early settlement
of the existing dispute, Hsu Shing-loh and L.T. Yuen in an
interview with Mr. Hopkins, President of the Company, stated
that they could get the men back to work if the Company
would promise to negotiate a settlement at an early date.
Mr. Hopkins advised the two gentlemen that as the Company
could not see its way clear to altering its attitude regarding
its obligations to its workers it would not be politic for
them to engage in a discussion or mediation likely to result
in failure as such failure would only help to complicate
the situation.

国家商业银行总经理徐星六（Hsu Shing-loh）、工部局华顾问阮维清（L.T. Yuen）和商会主席王筱籁（Wong Shafo-lai）以及其他许多知名华人组成一个委员会，并就尽早解决现有纠纷一事接触上海电力公司管理层。徐星六和阮维清在与公司董事长霍普金斯（Hopkins）先生的会晤中表示，如果公司承诺早日谈判解决，他们能让工人复工。霍普金斯先生告知两位先生，由于公司看不出有理由改变其对工人义务的态度，他们参与可能导致失败的讨论或调解是不明智的，因为这种失败只会使局势复杂化。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 179 So. O
Date 7 / November.
Date November 16, 1933.

Subject (in full) Shanghai Power Company - situation.

Made by D.S.I. Golder Forwarded by Whoever ASO

The situation in the various departments of the
Shanghai Power Company remains unchanged this morning.
The Company are at present employing 365 additional
foreigners distributed as follows:-
A) Riverside Power Station - 171 temporary Russians and
26 other Europeans.
B) Fearon Road Depot - 158 temporary Russians.
Temporary foreign employees are receiving $4.00 per day
on an average.

The meeting scheduled to take place in the office
of A.S. Fessenden at 11 a.m. November 15 was attended by
Mr. Hopkins, President of the Shanghai Power Company, Doo
Yueh Sung and Tsai Poh Ding, who acted as interpreter.
The representative of the Company outlined to Doo Yueh
Sung the offer to advance one month's pay (Vide report dated
15/11/33). In reply, Doo stated that he would convey
the proposal to the strikers and do everything to bring
about an early resumption of work.

Doo Yueh Sung's intervention in the present
dispute has been viewed with suspicion by the Company and
the Police, and it was learned from a confidential source
that Doo's mediation was motivated by a desire to control
Chinese labour in so far as it concerns foreign utility
companies in the Settlement, a sphere of commercial
activity hitherto comparatively free of his influence.

Doo Yueh Sung's attitude during the past few
days has led influential Chinese to contend that he is
anxious to lose sight of his past and is taking this
opportunity to appear in the role of a public benefactor .

(批：16/11)

主题（全称）上海电力公司 - 局势。

制作：副督察 Golder 转发： whoever ASO

今晨，上海电力公司各部门的局势保持不变。公司目前额外雇佣了365名外国人，分布如下：-
A) 江边发电厂 - 171名临时俄国人和26名其他欧洲人。
B) 斐伦路仓库 - 158名临时俄国人。
临时外籍雇员平均每天收入4.00美元。

原定于11月15日上午11时在 A.S. 费森登办公室举行的会议，出席者有上海电力公司董事长霍普金斯先生、杜月笙和担任翻译的蔡伯鼎（Tsai Poh Ding）。公司代表向杜月笙概述了预付一个月工资的提议（参见1933年11月15日报告）。作为回应，杜表示他将把这一提议传达给罢工者，并尽一切努力促使早日复工。

公司和警方对杜月笙介入当前纠纷持怀疑态度，并从机密渠道获悉，杜的调解动机是希望控制租界内外资公用事业公司的中国劳工，这是一个此前他的影响力相对较小的商业活动领域。

杜月笙过去几天的态度导致一些有影响力的华人认为，他急于让人忘记他的过去，并利用这个机会扮演公众恩人的角色。

（批注：11/16）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 8,. 1933

STRIKERS ASSAULT
BRITISH SUBJECT

Another Applicant For
Work At Power Co.
Intimidated

Another severe case of intimi-
dation by strikers of the Shang-
hai Power Company occurred yes-
terday. The victim was Mr.
James Muller, a Eurasian from
Hongkong and a British subject,
who applied for a position at the
Riverside plant of the Power
Company.
Shortly after leaving the plant
and while walking along Yang-
tzepoo Road near the old No. 9
Sung Sing cotton mill, Muller was
attacked by a gang of some 20
Chinese. He was severely beaten
and stabbed, but his condition was
subsequently described as not
serious by the authorities of the
Sacred Heart Hospital to which
he was taken. Mr. Muller was
wearing foreign style clothes when
attacked.
Yesterday was the date first set
by the Power Company for the
employment of men to take the
places vacated by the strikers.
More than 400 applications have
been received, and it is believed
that over 200 positions are open.
However, because of the intimida-
tion, it is said that the actual hir-
ing of the men has been postpon-
ed for a few days.
The vernacular press yesterday
stated that a meeting in regard
to the strike took place between
Mr. Sterling Fessenden, Secret-
ary-General of the S.M.C., and
Mr. Doo Yueh-sun of the Shang-
hai Municipality. Any results
were not announced.

（批：JMR 8/11）

罢工者袭击
英国臣民

又一名电力公司
求职申请人受恐吓

昨日又发生一起上海电力公司罢工者严重恐吓事件。受害者为詹姆斯·穆勒先生，系来自香港的欧亚混血儿，英国臣民，他曾向电力公司江边工厂申请职位。
穆勒离开工厂不久，在沿杨树浦路行走至旧松盛第九棉纱厂附近时，遭到一群约20名中国人的袭击。他遭到严重殴打和刺伤，但随后被送往的圣心医院当局称其伤势并不严重。穆勒遇袭时身着西式服装。
昨日是电力公司原定雇佣人员填补罢工者空缺岗位的首日。目前已收到400多份申请，据悉有200多个职位空缺。然而，由于受到恐吓，据说实际录用工作已推迟数日。
中文报纸昨日称，工部局秘书长费信惇（Sterling Fessenden）先生与上海市的杜月笙先生就罢工问题举行了会晤。未公布任何结果。

At 1.35 p.m. 7/11/33 a telephone message was
received from the Shanghai Fire Brigade to the
effect that they had taken a Eurasian named James
Miller to the Sacred Heart Hospital, suffering from
injuries received at the hands of a number of Chinese
on Yangtszepoo Road.

The undersigned immediately proceeded to the
Sacred Heart Hospital and interviewed the injured
man who gave the following particulars.

His age is 29, Single unemployed Marine Engineer,
British Eurasian born in Singapore of a Cantonese
mother and British father. He has no fixed abode
but when funds permit sleeps in the Hanbury Institute
at which place his passport was stolen from him short-
ly after his arrival in Shanghai about 2 years ago.
He is not registered at the British Consulate.

At about 10 a.m. to-day the complainant went to
the Riverside Power Station to apply for work and
after waiting outside for about 2 hours was told to
return later.

Having no money, he started to walk back to town
along Yangtszepoo Road and when about 300 yards east
of Lay Road Bridge or about 1 mile from Riverside
Power Station, 4 or 5 male Chinese who had been
walking behind him for some distance suddenly attacked
him. Almost immediately a number of other Chinese
appeared (about 20) and joined in the assault.

The complainant was severely punched and also
received two small wounds on the back probably
inflicted by a small pen knife.

Subject (in full) Reported intimidation of applicants for employment at

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Hillgoss

Sir,
At 9.50 a.m. 4/11/33 a telephone message was received from
C.D.S. 63 to the effect that applicants for employment at the
Riverside Power Station were being stopped and searched on Tengyueh
Road by strikers of the R.P.C..
A party of police under C/Inspector Foley immediately proceeded
to investigate and en route to Tengyueh Road, saw, on Yangtszepoo
Road about 10 yards east of Glen Road a group of about 3 people.
On enquiring, the party was told by two men who claimed to be
applicants for employment at the Riverside Power Station that
they had been stopped by strikers and their identification badges
taken away from them.
It would appear that applicants, after giving particulars of
their qualifications etc, are given a small cardboard disc
bearing a number and told to report on the 7th November 1933 to
see if they are suitable.
Whilst proceeding along Yangtszepoo Road on their way home
two of the applicants were stopped by strikers and on the arrival
of the police they pointed out a man whose name is Chiang Kung
Loong ( 蔣根隆 ), residing at No. 1 Wha Shing Faung off
Yangtszepoo Road as being one of the men who took their badges
from them.

报告

事由（全称）：关于罢工者恐吓 Riverside Power Station（江边发电厂）求职者的报告。

由 D.S.I. Hillgoss 制作并呈报

先生，
1933年11月4日上午9时50分，接到中央巡捕房63号电话消息，称 Riverside Power Station（江边发电厂）的求职者正在腾越路被 R.P.C.（上海电力公司）的罢工者拦截和搜身。
由 Foley 警督率领的一队警察立即前往调查，在前往腾越路途中，于杨树浦路格兰路以东约10码处，看到一群约3人。
经询问，两名自称是 Riverside Power Station（江边发电厂）求职者的男子告诉警方，他们被罢工者拦住，身份证牌被抢走。
看来，求职者在提供资格等详细信息后，会获得一个印有号码的小纸板圆牌，并被告知于1933年11月7日前来报到，以查看是否录用。
当这两名求职者在回家途中沿杨树浦路行走时，被罢工者拦住，警察到达后，他们指认一名叫 Chiang Kung Loong（蔣根隆）的男子是抢走他们牌证的人之一，该人居住在杨树浦路华兴坊1号。
两名投诉人和 Chiang Kung Loong 被带到巡捕房，其中一名投诉人作了如下陈述，另一名予以佐证。
“我叫 Woo Ah Saung（吳阿松），21岁，宁波人，住中山路35号。
我和我的朋友 Sung Ping Hwa（宋炳華），18岁，宁波人，住同一地址，于

Riverside Power Station at 6 a.m. 4/11/33 in order to obtain a
situation we were seen by a foreigner who took down our particulars
and after taking our thumb-prints gave us a cardboard badge. My
number was 117 and Sung Ping Hwa 115. We were told to return on
Tuesday 7/11/33 in order to find out whether we were to start
work or not.
We left the Power Station at 9.30 a.m. and were walking along
Yangtsepoo Road when two Chinese males approached, one later
arrested by Police and another wearing a foreign style cap.
These two men asked us if we had enrolled at the Shanghai
Power Company and on receiving a reply in the affirmative, asked
to see our badges. We refused, and the man in the cap then took
it off and showed us a number of similar badges, and asked if
ours were the same. After this they asked our number, and when
we took our badges out to see the numbers they were snatched by
the two men. The men then said that they were strikers of the
Power Company and told us not to go to work on Tuesday. At
the time of the conversation there was a large crowd of other
people around, most of whom seemed to be also strikers."
The accused denies that he took part in the act of which he
is accused and states that he was walking on Yangtsepoo Road and
saw a crowd and went to see what was the matter and while watching
was arrested.
He admits that he is a S.P.C. striker.
The D.O. "D" and the D.D.O. "L" were informed and after
reviewing the evidence available decided that it was too weak to
support a charge.
Further, the complainants refuse to proceed against the accused.
Therefore the accused has been severely cautioned and released.

1933年11月4日上午6时前往 Riverside Power Station（江边发电厂）谋求职位。我们被一名外国人叫住，他记录了我们的详细信息，在采集了指纹后给了我们一个纸板牌证。我的号码是117，Sung Ping Hwa 的是115。我们被告知于1933年11月7日（星期二）回来，以确定是否开始工作。
我们上午9时30分离开发电厂，沿杨树浦路行走时，两名中国男子上前搭话，其中一人后来被警察逮捕，另一人戴着西式帽子。
这两人问我们是否在上海电力公司登记报名，得到肯定答复后，要求看我们的牌证。我们拒绝了，戴帽子的男子随后摘下帽子，向我们展示了许多类似的牌证，问我们的是否一样。之后他们询问我们的号码，当我们拿出牌证查看号码时，牌证被这两人抢走。这些人随后说他们是电力公司的罢工者，告诉我们星期二不要去上班。谈话时周围有一大群人，其中大多数人似乎也是罢工者。”
被告否认参与被指控的行为，并称他当时正走在杨树浦路上，看到一群人便上前查看情况，在围观时被逮捕。
他承认自己是 S.P.C.（上海电力公司）的罢工者。
已通知 “D” 区警官和 “L” 区副警官，在审查现有证据后，认为证据太弱，不足以支持起诉。
此外，投诉人拒绝对被告提起诉讼。
因此，被告受到严厉警告后被释放。

他被告知，如果他在11月7日报到上班，将面临被枪击的危险。
此人立即返回 Riverside Power Station（江边发电厂），肯定在凌晨1点前到达那里，但直到上午11点才通知警方，当时具名人亲自通过电话获悉此事。

The compl...nt is a unemployed fitter and at
.. .. the 6/11/33 went to the riverside power
station to seek employment. His particulars were
taken and he was told to report again on the 7/11/33.
He did so and waited outside until about 11 a.m. when
he was told he would not be needed today. He then
started to walk home via Jingliang Road via Yiping,
Clos and Jingliang Roads and on arriving at Jiangwu
road corner, was suddenly seized from behind by the
accused and two others who commenced to punch him and
at the same time told him that he was not to go to
work at the motor company.

The complainant broke away from his assailants
and ran along Jiangwu road pursued by the three men
and after running about 100 yards turned left and ran
across a field pursued by the accused only. After
running across the field for about 50 yards the compt
was again seized by the accused who threw him to the
ground and repeatedly punched him in the back.

While the two men were running across the field
the undersigned and Mr. Black were passing along
Jingliang Road in a car and they stopped and ran to
the complainant's assistance and arrested the accused
who was attempting to escape.

The accused admits that he assaulted the complt.
and stated that he did so because he was told to do
so by his Labour Union.

He has been charged with intimidation contrary
to Article 318 of the C.C.R.C. and will appear before
the S.S.D.C. on the 9/11/33.

投诉人是一名失业的装配工，于
1933年11月6日前往江边发电厂
求职。他的详细信息被记录，并被告知于1933年11月7日再次报到。
他照做了，并在外面等到约上午11时，当时
他被告知今天不需要他。于是他
开始经靖江路、逸平路、Clos 路和靖江路步行回家，当到达江武路拐角时，
突然被被告和另外两人从背后抓住，他们开始殴打他，
同时告诉他不得去汽车公司上班。

投诉人挣脱了袭击者，
沿江武路逃跑，后面有三个人追赶，
跑了约100码后向左转，穿过一块田地，只有被告一人追赶。
在田地里跑了约50码后，投诉人
再次被被告抓住，被告将他摔倒在地，并反复殴打他的背部。

当这两人跑过田地时，
具名人和 Black 先生正乘车经过靖江路，他们停车并跑去
帮助投诉人，逮捕了试图逃跑的被告。

被告承认殴打了投诉人，
并称他这样做是因为工会命令他这么做。

他被控违反《中华民国刑法》第318条进行恐吓，将于1933年11月9日出庭 S.S.D.C. 法庭。

Complainant is a foreman carpenter at present
without employment and on the morning of the 4th.
November 1933 went to Riverside Power Station and
applied for a situation. His particulars were
taken and he was given a cardboard identification
disc and told to report again on the 6th. Nov. 1933.
When returning home along Yangtzepoo Road at
8.30 a.m. on the 4th. inst. he was stopped by about
15 strikers one of whom took away his identification
disc and he was told that if he returned to the
Power Station he would be shot.
Complainant immediately returned to the Power
Station and reported the occurrence and subsequently
the report was passed to the Police. The above was
briefly recorded in Misc. File 316 (Y) 4.11/33.
About 8 a.m. this morning the complainant
walked along Yangtzepoo Road in the hope of meeting
the man who had taken his disc and when near
Tongyuch Road he saw the accused and others.
The accused approached the complainant and
repeated the warning given on the 4th. Nov. 1933
and the complainant seized him and blew a Police
whistle but the accused escaped before the arrival
of Police.
The complainant remained in the vicinity of
the Power Station Gate until shortly before 1 a.m.
and then boarded an omnibus and proceeded to
Yangchow Road where he resides.
The accused and several other strikers travelled
on the same vehicle and alighted at Yangchow Road

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

The complainant is a wharf coolie at present
unemployed and at 6.3 a.m. to-day went to the
Riverside Power Station to seek employment.
Whilst waiting outside the Tongting Road
entrance to the Power Station he was approached by
the two accused and another not arrested and ordered
to go away from the Station and not apply for
work.

The two accused to enforce their order commenced
to assault the complainant by punching him with their
fists. The complainant fell to the ground and the
accused continued to assault by kicking him.

While the assault was in progress Mr. Easting
an engineer employed at the Riverside Power Station
emerged from the gate and seized the accused and
held them until the arrival of the I. M. Co. 75 & 113
who were on duty at Tongting and Yangtzepoo Roads
corner.

The complainant who complained of bruises of
the back and side was sent to the Sacred Heart
Hospital, Mingkwo Road, and doctor's certificate
was issued as follows: "No surgical wounds."

The accused are strikers of the Riverside Power
Station and deny that they assaulted the complainant.
They stated that they intended to return to work.

The assault was witnessed by Mr. Easting and
I. M. Co. 75 113 and the accused are charged with
assault contrary to Article 293 of the C.C.R.C. and
further charged with intimidation contrary to Article
318 of C.C.R.C., the latter charge forming the
subject of F.I.R. 744/33(Y).

报案人目前是一名失业的码头苦力，于今天上午6:30前往杨树浦发电厂求职。
当他在发电厂洞庭路入口外等候时，两名被告及另一名未被捕者走近他，命令他离开发电厂并不准申请工作。

为了强制执行他们的命令，两名被告开始用拳头殴打报案人。报案人倒在地上，被告继续踢打他。

在殴打进行时，受雇于杨树浦发电厂的工程师 Easting 先生从大门走出，抓住被告并将其控制住，直到在洞庭路与杨树浦路拐角处执勤的印捕75号和113号到达。

报案人诉称背部和侧面有瘀伤，被送往民国路圣心医院，医生出具的证明如下：“无外科伤口。”

被告是杨树浦发电厂的罢工者，否认殴打了报案人。他们表示打算回去工作。

Easting 先生和印捕75号、113号目睹了此次殴打，被告被指控违反《中华民国刑法》第293条之殴打罪，并被进一步指控违反《中华民国刑法》第318条之恐吓罪，后一项指控构成首次情报报告 744/33(Y) 的主题。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 8, 1933

POWER COMPANY
STRIKE
More Intimidators Arrested and
Fined by Court

Continued efforts of attempted
intimidation of the Shanghai Power
Company's new employees by the
company's strikers resulted in three
more of the latter being charged in
the First Special District Court
yesterday morning. The accused
were each fined $20 by the Court, or,
alternatively, 20 days' imprison-
ment.
The charges against the three
men yesterday were that they had
resorted to violence and used
threats in their attempt to prevent
the company's loyal workers from
going to work. They were arrested
by officers of Yangtszepoo Station.
Three intimidators were already
fined by the Court on Monday morn-
ing also for attempting to prevent
the new workers from starting to
work.

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be commented on by investigating officer).

The complainant is a wharf coolie at present unemployed and at 6.3 a.m. to-day went to the Riverside Power Station to seek employment.

Whilst waiting outside the Tongting Road entrance to the Power Station he was approached by the two accused and another not arrested and ordered to go away from the station and not apply for work.

The two accused to enforce their order commenced to assault the complainant by punching him with their fists. The complainant fell to the ground and the accused continued the assault by kicking him.

While the assault was in progress Mr. Fasting an engineer employed at the Riverside Power Station emerged from the gate and seized the accused and held them until the arrival of the J.P.Co. 75 & 113 who were on duty at Tongting and Yangtsepoo Roads corner.

The complainant who complained of bruises of the back and side was sent to the Sacred Heart Hospital, Mingkuo Road, and doctor's certificate was issued as follows: "No surgical wounds."

The accused are strikers of the Riverside Power Station and deny that they assaulted the complainant. They state that they intended to return to work.

The assault was witnessed by Mr. Fasting and J.P.Co. 75 and 113 and the accused are charged with intimidation contrary to Article 318 of the C.C.R.C

REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY. File No. ______ No. D Date ______）
Date November 6, 1933.
Subject (in full) Shanghai Power Company - arrest of 3 ex-workers by
Kashing Road Station for intimidation.
Made by D.S.I. Golder Forwarded by Ja Prince
At 11.15 a.m. on Saturday, November 4, whilst at
the Shanghai Power Company office, Nanking Road, on my routine
daily visit I was informed that 3 men had been arrested
in Kashing Road District for having intimidate a Chinese
for having applied to the Shanghai Power Company for
employment.
I proceeded to Kashing Road and with the
assistance of a Senior Chinese detective questioned the
three men in custody. They freely admitted the offence
but claimed in extenuation of their action that they
were only protecting their own livelihood in preventing
outsiders from taking their jobs. All three were
persons of limited intelligence and appeared somewhat
hazy as to the gravity of the offence of which they
were guilty.
From the outset the complainant in the case
stoutly refused to prosecute for fear of later reprisals,
he was, however, later persuaded to sign the F.I.R. relative
to the case and to sign a statement.
D.S.I. Palmer, Senior Detective of Kashing Road,
was at first instructed by the Officer i/c of 'C' Division
to release the men in view of the complainant's attitude,
but before such instructions were executed, Mr. Aiers, D.C.
Divisions, following a conversation with Mr. R.T. Bryan,
Municipal Advocate, issued instructions that the men be
charged.
As a result of the foregoing instructions all three
were charged and appeared at Court on Monday, November 6, when
they were each fined $20.00.

报告
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 刑事与特别股登记处。档案号 ______ 第 D 号 日期 ______）
日期 1933 年 11 月 6 日。
主题（全称）上海电力公司 - 嘉善路警署因恐吓罪逮捕 3 名前工人。
呈报人 副督察长 Golder 转呈人 Ja Prince
11 月 4 日星期六上午 11:15，当我在南京路上海电力公司办公室进行日常例行巡视时，获悉有 3 名男子在嘉善路辖区被捕，原因是恐吓一名向上海电力公司申请工作的华人。

我随即前往嘉善路，并在一名高级华探的协助下讯问了这三名在押男子。他们坦率地承认了罪行，但为其行为辩解称，他们只是为了防止外人抢走他们的工作，从而保护自己的生计。这三人都智力有限，似乎对自己所犯罪行的严重性有些模糊不清。

从一开始，本案报案人就因担心日后遭到报复而坚决拒绝起诉，但他后来被说服签署了与此案相关的初步调查报告（F.I.R.）并签署了一份陈述书。

嘉善路高级侦探 Palmer 副督察长起初接到“C”分区主管警官的指示，鉴于报案人的态度，释放这些人，但在执行该指示之前，分区副总监 Alers 先生在与市政检察官 R.T. Bryan 先生交谈后，发出指示要求对这些男子提出指控。

根据上述指示，三人均被起诉，并于 11 月 6 日星期一出庭，每人被罚款 20.00 元。

At 9.15 a.m. 4-11-33, at the request of complainant Woo Tsing Zai (吳俊才), C.P.Cs. 2141 and 3192 brought to the station the above described accused whom complainant stated had attempted to force him to accompany them to the Shanghai Power Company Strikers' Union, Chapei.

Enquiries by D.S.I. Chu, C.D.C. 297 and the undersigned learned that at about 9 a.m. even date complainant and his friend named Sung Kwen Ziang (沈桂祥), taking advantage of the strike of the Shanghai Power Company's workers, proceeded to the Shanghai Power Company, Fearon Road, to seek a position. Upon arrival, they were interviewed by a foreigner who instructed them to return when the strike finished. When leaving the Company's premises, they observed about 30 agitators who demanded to know why they had been seeking employment when all the workers were on strike. Complainant stated he immediately walked away and upon arriving at at the entrance to the Li Hongkew Ka (裏虹口街), East Hanbury Road, the three accused and others set upon him and informed him that they were going to take him to the Shanghai Power Company's Strikers' Union, Tiendong Road, Chapei, where they would put him to death. At this juncture a Chinese policeman approached causing the accused and their companions to decamp. Complainant then proceeded to board the 18th Route railless car, but was again seized by the accused (the C.P.C. having walked away) and pulled into the Li Hongkew Ka (裏虹口街) and forced to accompany them. pages.en:
Woo Tsing Zai

Shanghai                                D.S.I. Wong Zung Ying
K.Rd. Stn.          4-11-33             Clerk Li Yang Kau.

My name is Woo Tsing Zai, 26 years, native of Shanghai,
Married and my parents are all alive. I am a brass-smith,
residing at 6 Dau Ka Wen, Pi Hong Road, Chapei. I am now
employed at the Brass-smiths' Department of the China Electrical
Co., earning $1.20 per day.

I know a Cantonese woman, whose husband is a foreigner
employed at the Shanghai Power Company's godown, Fearon Road.
I asked the Cantonese woman some time ago to speak to the
foreigner if he could get a job for me in the Power Company and
she replied she would.

Last month, the employees of the Power Company went on
strike and at about 7 p.m. yesterday, the Cantonese woman,
afore-mentioned, came to my home and requested me to go and
see the foreigner in the Power Company, Fearon Road.

At about 7 a.m. today, I asked a neighbour of mine, named
Sung Kwen Ziang, native of Shanghai, also a brass-smith, now
unemployed, to go with me. After we had seen the foreigner,
we and 2 others not known were brought to see the manager.
After explaining our object of paying this visit to him, the
manager told us that 4 of us were not enough to be employed at
present to take up all the work that had been left behind and
said he would notify us again when the trouble was over. We
then left his office and when we came out of the factory, we
saw more than 30 men of the worker type, all in short clothing
and looked so fierce, standing outside. When they saw us, they
immediately gathered around us and asked us, saying, "Why are
you coming here to get your jobs, the strike is not over yet?"
pages.zh:
吴清仔（音译）

上海                                副巡官 黄宗英（音译）
昆山路站          1933年11月4日     书记员 李杨高（音译）

本人名叫吴清仔（音译），26岁，上海籍，
已婚，父母均健在。本人系铜匠，
居住于闸北辟鸿路豆家文6号。本人现受雇于
中国电气公司铜匠部，日薪1.20元。

本人认识一名广东籍女子，其丈夫为外国人，
受雇于斐伦路上海电力公司仓库。
前一段时间，本人曾请该广东籍女子向该外国人询问，
能否在电力公司为本人谋得一份工作，
她答复说可以帮忙。

上月，电力公司员工举行罢工，昨日傍晚约7时，
前述广东籍女子来到本人家中，要求本人前往
斐伦路电力公司见那名外国人。

今日上午约7时，本人邀请一位邻居，名叫宋坤祥（音译），
上海籍，亦为铜匠，目前失业，与本人同行。我们见过那名外国人后，
本人与另外两名身份不明者被带去见经理。
在向经理说明此次来访的目的后，
经理告知我们，目前仅凭我们四人不足以承担所有积压的工作，
并表示待风波平息后会再通知我们要否复工。随后我们离开其办公室，
当我们走出工厂时，看见外面站着三十多名工人模样的男子，
均着短衣，神情凶狠。他们看见我们后，
立即围拢过来质问我们：“罢工尚未结束，你们为何来此求职？”

pages.en:
Woo Tsing Zai.

On hearing same, I became to feel afraid that some thing
undesirous to us might happen, So I immediately slipped away.
I walked past East Yuhang Road Bridge and turning right to
East Hanbury Road Bridge, I later arrived at the place where
the bus stop. But I was approached by three unknown persons
at the entrance to Li Hongkew Ku, who caught hold of me and
started to pull me away. I struggled with them and they
started to assault me . During the assault, my grey felt hat
fell on the ground and was taken away by someone unknown. They
said that they wanted to take me to the Union Headquarters of
the Shanghai Power Company's workers on Tiendong Road, Chapei.
If I refused to go, they said they would treat me with violence.
I was so afraid and just at this time, a Chinese Policeman,
who was coming along East Hanbury Road, came up and drove the
three persons who had had me in their custody and several
others who were following, away. As I saw that it was time
for me to get away, I immediately boarded an 18th Route rail-
less car. But unexpectedly that the three men, who saw that
the Chinese policeman had walked away, came up and dragged me
down. They then pulled me into the Li Hongkew Ku. As I was
at this time alone and helpless, I could do nothing but
follow them along East Yuhang Road and when at the corner of
East Yalu and Wuchow Roads, I saw another policeman. I
immediately called upon the Policeman to rescue me. Two
Chinese Policemen then came up to us and after I had told them
all that had taken place, they brought all of us to the Police
Station.

Signed, Woo Tsing Zai.
pages.zh:
吴清仔（音译）。

闻听此言，本人担心会发生对本人不利之事，遂立即溜走。
本人走过东余杭路桥，右转至东汉伯利路桥，随后到达公交车站附近。
但在黎洪口库（音译）入口处，三名身份不明者接近本人，
抓住本人并试图将本人拖走。本人与其挣扎，他们便开始殴打本人。
在殴打过程中，本人的灰色毡帽掉落在地，被某名身份不明者拿走。
他们称要将本人带往闸北天通庵路15号俊英坊（音译）的上海电力公司工人联合会总部。
他们表示，若本人拒绝前往，将对本人施以暴力。
本人十分恐惧，恰在此时，一名沿东汉伯利路走来的中国警察上前，
驱散了控制本人的那三人以及跟随的其他几人。本人见机不可失，
立即登上一辆18路无轨电车。不料那三人见中国警察已走开，
又追上来将本人拉下车。随后他们将本人拖入黎洪口库（音译）。
当时本人孤立无援，别无他法，只能随他们沿东余杭路前行。
当行至鸭绿江路（音译）与梧州路转角处时，本人看见另一名警察。
本人立即呼救请求警察解救。随后两名中国警察来到现场，
在本人陈述事发经过后，他们将所有人带至警察局。

签署人：吴清仔（音译）

pages.en:
Hyui Hoong Zien, C.P.C. 2141.

K.Rd. Stn.           4-11-33           Clerk Li Yang Kao.

On the forenoon of the 4-11-33, I was on 8 beat duty and
at 9.05 a.m. whilst I was walking from Wuchow Road market to
the corner of East Yalu and Wuchow Roads, I saw three male
Chinese pulling another male Chinese along Wuchow Road in a
Northerly direction. On hearing the alarm raised by the man
who was being pulled by the other three, I immediately went
up to the scene and after questioning them the cause of the
trouble, I brought the both parties to the station.

Signed, Hyui Hoong Zien.
pages.zh:
许宏先（音译），华捕编号 2141。

昆山路站           1933年11月4日           书记员 李杨高（音译）

1933年11月4日上午，本人在第8巡逻区执勤，
上午9时05分，当本人从梧州路市场走向鸭绿江路（音译）与梧州路转角处时，
看见三名中国男子沿梧州路向北方向拖拽另一名中国男子。
听到被拖拽男子的呼救声后，本人立即赶赴现场，
在询问纠纷起因后，将双方带至警局。

签署人：许宏先（音译）

pages.en:
Zee Ling Nyoen. C.P.C. 3192.

K.Rd. Stn.          4-11-33          Clerk Li Yang Kao.

On the forenoon of the 4-11-33, I was on post duty at the
corner of Wuchow and East Yalu Roads. At 9.05 a.m. I perceived
that three men were pulling another man along Wuchow Road in a
Northerly direction and when they were passing the corner of
Wuchow and East Yalu Roads, the man, who was being pulled by
the others, called upon the Police to rescue him. C.P.C. 2141
and myself immediately went up and after having ascertained the
cause of their trouble, we brought the both parties to the
Station.

Signed, Zee Ling Nyoen, C.P.C. 3192.

徐林源（音译），华捕编号 3192。

昆山路站          1933年11月4日          书记员 李杨高（音译）

1933年11月4日上午，本人在梧州路与鸭绿江路（音译）转角处岗哨执勤。
上午9时05分，本人察觉三名男子正沿梧州路向北方向拖拽另一名男子，
当他们经过梧州路与鸭绿江路（音译）转角处时，
被拖拽的男子呼喊警察求救。华捕编号2141与本人立即上前，
在查明纠纷起因后，将双方带至警局。

签署人：徐林源（音译），华捕编号 3192。

pages.en:
Zung Ah Shing.
Pootung                                C.D.C. 297 Zung Kying Sung.
K. Rd. Stn.          4-11-33           Clerk: Li Yang Kao.

My name is Zung Ah Shing, 24, native of Pootung, M/brass-
smith, residing at House No. 12, Lane 37, Thorne Road.
During September of the 19th year of the Chinese Republic
(1930), a foreman named Wang Ah Ching of the Brass-smith's
Department of the Power Company, Pearson Road, introduced me to
the Power Company to be Brass-smith No. B26 and I have been
employed there for just three years. On the 1-10-33, all the
workers of the Power Company's new factory at Yangtzepoo went
on strike. Later the strikers from the latter place went to
the various branch factories of the Power Company to ask the
employees there to join the strike. It has been more than a
month since I joined. At 7.30 a.m. on the 4-11-33, I went to
Li Hongkew Ka to take some food, after which I went to a tea-
shop on the same road to take tea. At 9.30 a.m. I left the
teashop and proceeded to the Power Company's factory on Pearson
Road to see if any one returned to the factory to work. At
about 9 a.m. I saw a man coming out of the factory. I immediat
ly followed him to East Hanbury Road Bridge, where I caught hold
of him (Woo Tsing Zai, the complainant), and asked him to go to
the Power Co's. Workers' Union at 15 Zoen Yuin Fong, Tien-dong
Road, Chapel. Complainant then called a Chinese policeman, who
came up and drove all of us away, saying that we were not allow
ed to cause any trouble on the road. Complainant immediately
boarded an 18th Route railless car, but three of us again went
up and dragged him down. When we were walking along Yalu Road
near Wuchow Road, the complainant raised an alarm, this was
heard by two Chinese policemen, who immediately came to his
pages.zh:
钟阿兴（音译）。
浦东                                侦缉警长 钟景松（音译）
昆山路站          1933年11月4日      书记员：李杨高（音译）

本人名叫钟阿兴（音译），24岁，浦东籍，职业铜匠，
居住于索恩路（音译）37弄12号。
民国十九年（1930年）九月，经皮尔逊路电力公司铜匠部工头王阿清（音译）介绍，
本人进入电力公司担任B26号铜匠，至今已满三年。
1933年10月1日，杨树浦电力公司新厂全体工人罢工。
随后，该地罢工工人前往电力公司各分厂，要求当地员工加入罢工。
本人加入罢工已逾一月。1933年11月4日上午7时30分，
本人前往黎洪口卡（音译）进食，随后在同一路的茶馆饮茶。
上午9时30分，本人离开茶馆，前往皮尔逊路电力公司工厂，
查看是否有人回厂复工。上午约9时，本人看见一人走出工厂。
本人立即跟随其至东汉伯利路桥，在那里抓住了此人（即投诉人吴清仔），
并要求其前往闸北天通庵路15号俊英坊（音译）的电力公司工人联合会。
投诉人随即呼叫一名中国警察，警察上前将我们驱散，
称不得在路上滋事。投诉人立即登上一辆18路无轨电车，
但我们三人再次上前将其拉下车。当我们沿鸭绿江路（音译）靠近梧州路行走时，
投诉人发出呼救，两名中国警察听到后，立即前来

pages.en:
Van Loong Poh.
Haimun
C.D.S. 304 Yang Sih Kwang.
K.Rd. Stn.
4-11-33
Clerk Li Yang Kao.

My name is Van Loong Poh, 33 years, native of Haimun,
married, residing at 59 Pi Hoong Road, Hongtseng, Chapei.
During the 18th year of the Republic of China (1929), I was
introduced to the Power Co. by a friend of mine named Zung
Khong Zien and I was then employed as a coolie at the Company's
Branch Office, Haiphong Road. My number is 6CH 8. and am
getting $19 per month as my wages. During the 10th month of
this year, all the employees of the Company went on strike
and I also joined. Later I went to work on the roads in Chapei
as a coolie. On the 3-11-33, my friend Wong Ping Sung (3rd
accused) told me that a meeting was to be held at the Union
Headquarters today, 4-11-33 and asked me to attend same with
him. At 3 a.m. today, 4-11-33, Wong Ping Sung and I left our
homes and when we arrived at East Hanbury Road Bridge, we saw
more than persons quarrelling there. We then went up and found
that the complainant in this case wanted to get a job in the
Power Co. So Wang Ping Sung, myself and one other unknown to
me caught hold of the man (complainant) and decided to take him
to our Union at 15 Zoen Ying Fong, Tien-dong Road, Chapei to be
dealt with. But when were near the corner of East Yalu and
Wuchow Roads, we were arrested by the Police and brought to the
Police Station. The above is a true statement.

Signed and thumb printed by
Van Loong Poh
pages.zh:
范龙波（音译）。
海门
侦缉警士 杨世光（音译）
昆山路站
1933年11月4日
书记员 李杨高（音译）

本人名叫范龙波（音译），33岁，海门籍，
已婚，居住于闸北虹镇辟鸿路59号。
民国十八年（1929年），经朋友钟康先（音译）介绍，
本人进入电力公司，在海防路分公司办事处担任苦力。
本人编号为6CH 8，月薪19元。
今年十月，公司全体员工罢工，本人亦加入。
随后本人在闸北道路上做苦力谋生。
1933年11月3日，朋友黄平松（音译）（第三被告）告知本人，
今日（1933年11月4日）将在联合会总部召开会议，
邀本人一同参加。今日（1933年11月4日）凌晨3时，
黄平松与本人离家，抵达东汉伯利路桥时，
看见多人在那里争吵。我们上前查看，发现本案投诉人
欲在电力公司求职。于是黄平松、本人及另一名身份不明者
抓住该男子（投诉人），决定将其带往闸北天通庵路15号俊英坊（音译）
的联合会进行处理。但当我们就近行至鸭绿江路（音译）与梧州路转角处时，
被警察逮捕并带至警察局。以上陈述属实。

范龙波（音译）签字并按手印

pages.en:
Wong Ping Sung.
Shanghai                                C.D.S. 304 Yang Sih Kwang.
K.Rd. Stn.          4-11-33              Clerk Li Yang Kao

My name is Wong Ping Sung, 34 years, native of Shanghai,
married, residing at 15 Fi Hong Road, Hongtseng, Chapei.
During the 15th year of the Chinese Republic (1926), a friend
of mine named Tsang Sing Jien, a coolie employed at the Shang-
hai Power Co., introduced me to the same company and I was since
that time employed as a coolie No. WOK 3, at Company's Branch
Office, Haiphong Road. I am getting $17 every month as my
wages. During the 10th month this year all the employees of
the Company went on strike, so I have to stay at home and
think of some other means to obtain money. My present busi-
ness is to sell vegetables. On the 3-11-33, a friend of mine
named Tsang Sung Sung came and told me that I need not sell
vegetables again and as a number of workers of the Company
would return to work, he said that I could resume my work too.
So, at 8 a.m. today, 4-11-33, Van Loong Foh and I left our
homes and proceeded to East Hanbury Road Bridge, where we
saw a number of other workers of the Company who were quarrel-
ling. Van Loong Foh and I then went up and asked them what
their trouble was. On ascertaining that the complainant wished
to get a job in the Company, Van and myself and one other
unknown to me started to pull complainant along with intent to
take him to our Union at 15 Zoen Ying Fong, Tien-dong Road,
Chapei. But when we were near the corner of East Yalu and
Wuchow Roads we were arrested and brought to the Police station.
The above is a true statement.

Signed and thumb printed by Wong Ping Sung.
pages.zh:
黄平松（音译）。
上海                                侦缉警士 杨世光（音译）
昆山路站          1933年11月4日              书记员 李杨高（音译）

本人名叫黄平松（音译），34岁，上海籍，
已婚，居住于闸北虹镇斐鸿路15号。
民国十五年（1926年），经朋友曾胜坚（音译）介绍，
此人系上海电力公司苦力，本人由此进入该公司，
自此在海防路分公司办事处担任WOK 3号苦力。
本人月薪17元。今年十月，公司全体员工罢工，
本人只得居家另谋生计。本人目前以卖菜为业。
1933年11月3日，朋友曾松松（音译）前来告知本人，
无需再卖菜，因公司将有多名工人复工，
他表示本人也可恢复工作。
因此，今日（1933年11月4日）上午8时，范龙福（音译）与本人离家，
前往东汉伯利路桥，在那里看见多名其他公司工人正在争吵。
范龙福与本人上前询问纠纷缘由。
在得知投诉人希望在公司求职后，范某、本人及另一名身份不明者
开始拖拽投诉人，意图将其带往闸北天通庵路15号俊英坊（音译）的联合会。
但当我们就近行至鸭绿江路（音译）与梧州路转角处时，
被逮捕并带至警察局。以上陈述属实。

Fm. 12
Ca 10400-35-32

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & C. D. REGISTRY. File No. 154/33）
REPORT
Kashing Road Station,
Date November 1, 1933

Subject (in full) Re alleged intimidation of an employee of the Shanghai Power Company.
Made by D.S.I. Palmer. Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,
At 7.50 a.m. 1-11-33, a telephone message was received from Yangtszpoo Police Station to the effect that one of the employees of the Shanghai Power Company, residing at RC 351 Hailar Road had been intimidated.
Enquiries were made by C.D.C. 332 who ascertained that one Kyeong Siau Mau (熊小毛), an employee of the Shanghai Power Co., who was also one of the strikers, had resumed his work on 29-10-33. As he was afraid that the others still on strike would cause trouble to him, he stayed in the Company's premises.
At about 10 a.m. on the 31-10-33, a male Chinese, who represented himself to be a member of the strikers' Union, went to Kyeong's home at 351 Hailar Road to look for him. On finding that Kyeong was not there, the intruder said to his wife, Kyeong Li Sz (熊李氏), that her husband should be notified to leave his job right away and if he failed, all the members of the Union would come and see him.
（批：host / Kinghan / 1/11/33）
At about 12 noon the same day (31-10-33) another male Chinese called at Kyeong's home and his wife was again warned.
On being thus approached, the woman became afraid and went to the Shanghai Power Co. in the afternoon with intent to inform her husband, but she did not see him there. At about 6 a.m. today (1-11-33) she again proceeded to the aforementioned Company and informed her husband of the occurrence, who in turn reported the matter to the management of the Company and the Police were then informed.
When questioned by C.D.C. 332, the woman, Kyeong Li Sz, stated that since the second visit at 12 noon yesterday (31-10-33), no one had called at her home again.
pages.zh:
表格 12
案件编号 10400-35-32

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 中央及侦探处登记室。档案号 154/33）
报告
嘉善路警察局，
日期 1933年11月1日

事由（全称）关于涉嫌恐吓上海电力公司一名员工一事。
由副巡官帕尔默（Palmer）呈报。转呈人 [签名]

先生，
1933年11月1日上午7时50分，接到杨树浦警察局电话消息，
称居住于海拉尔路RC 351号的上海电力公司一名员工受到恐吓。
经侦缉警士编号332调查，查明上海电力公司员工熊小毛（Kyeong Siau Mau）
也是罢工者之一，已于1933年10月29日复工。
因担心其他仍在罢工的同事会找他麻烦，他留在公司 premises（厂区/宿舍）内。
1933年10月31日上午约10时，一名自称是罢工联合会成员的中国男子
前往海拉尔路351号熊小毛家中寻找他。
发现熊小毛不在家后，闯入者对其妻子熊李氏（Kyeong Li Sz）表示，
应通知其丈夫立即离职，否则联合会全体成员将前来找他。
（批注：host / Kinghan / 1933年11月1日）
同日（1933年10月31日）中午约12时，另一名中国男子到访熊家，
其妻子再次受到警告。
遭到此类滋扰后，该女子心生恐惧，于下午前往上海电力公司，
意图告知其丈夫，但未能在公司见到他。
今日（1933年11月1日）上午约6时，她再次前往上述公司，
将此事告知其丈夫，其丈夫随即向公司管理层报告，
警方随后获知此事。
经侦缉警士编号332讯问，女子熊李氏表示，
自昨日（1933年10月31日）中午第二次到访后，
再无他人到访其家中。

Subject (in full) S. P. C. Worker Threatened.

Made by D.S. White, Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At about 4.15.p.m. on the 31-10-33 Mr. Roach, S.P.C., brought to the station a female r. Tse Tsang Sz (朱張氏) residing at an unnumbered house in Jin Ka Pang, Ward Road, who reported that at about 2.30.p.m. on the 31st inst. a male Chinese called at her house and informed her that if her husband Tse Kyon Dung (朱家同) employed as a foreman in the J.P.C., Fearon Road Depot, continued to work instead of remaining on strike he would assault him; after this, the Chinese left the premises. Tse Tsang Sz also left a few minutes later with the intention of going to Fearon Road Depot to tell her husband, when she again met this man who again told her that her husband would be assaulted if he carried on work.

When she arrived at the depot she told her husband, and he reported the affair to those i/c of depot; who advised both man and wife that they should report the occurrence to the police station concerned, at the same time stating that theirs was the third case of similar nature that had been reported to them.

The following is the description of the unknown Chinese.
Age about 35-36.
Height about 5'6"
Round face, dark complexion.
Medium build, wearing blue jacket and pants, black cap.
speaking Shanghai dialect.

The above description was given by Tse Tsang Sz.

C.P.C.s warned to keep the place under observation.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
[Signature]

Subject (in full) Shanghai Power Company - Statement of Zung Ching-loh
(陳慶祿), Clerk, who was shot and wounded in
Chinese Territory on October 20, 1933.

Made by D.S.I. Golder Forwarded by Whouncan D.S.I.

With reference to the statement of Zung Ching-loh,
Stores Accountant's Clerk of the Shanghai Power Company,
(attached), who was shot and wounded on the Ma Yue San
Road on the morning of October 20, 1933.

When first questioned on November 8, Zung was
recovering from the effects of an anaesthetic administered
to him earlier that day and as a consequence was not very
clear on the subject of the attempt upon his life.
Further interrogation on November 13, to some extent,
clears up the points on which further information was
necessary but beyond giving a fairly detailed account
of the affair from the time he was first accosted outside
his own house the victim is unable to offer any really
useful information. He claims that he does not
know the name of the man who was responsible for the
shooting nor does he know of anyone who could possibly
be connected with the plot to take his life.

He states that after informing him that he was
wanted at the General Labour Union for the purpose of
talking to Wu Tsu-bai (吳祖培), the three men who
approached him near his home, followed him to the Union
and asked him to wait in the Meeting Hall which is
situated at the rear of the General Labour Union premises
(see sketch attached).

After the four had waited in this room for some
five minutes the person No.3 described as being unknown
to Zung, left the room and went into the Reception Room
to the East which at that time was being used as a
Communication Office by the Fourth District Water and

制作人 副督察长 Golder 转呈人 Whouncan 副督察长

关于上海电力公司仓库会计职员陈庆禄（Zung Ching-loh）的陈述（见附件），他于1933年10月20日上午在马玉山路（Ma Yue San Road，音译）被枪击受伤。

11月8日首次讯问时，陈庆禄正从当天早些时候接受的麻醉剂影响中恢复，因此对此次未遂谋杀案的细节记忆不是很清晰。
11月13日的进一步讯问在一定程度上澄清了需要补充信息的几点，但除了相当详细地叙述了从他在自家门外首次被人搭讪开始的经过外，受害者无法提供任何真正有用的信息。他声称不知道开枪者的姓名，也不知道有任何人可能与企图杀害他的阴谋有关。

他说，那三名在他家附近接近他的男子告诉他，总工会找他是要与吴祖培（Wu Tsu-bai）谈话，随后他们跟随他来到工会，并要求他在位于总工会 premises 后方的会议厅等待（见附图）。

or five persons were in the Reception Room and that he
could hear them conversing in low tones but was unable
to distinguish what was being said.    Following the
departure from the room of the stranger, Zung sat waiting
for a further five minutes, at the end of that time the
man returned followed by the would-be murderer.    The
two came over to where Zung, Ah Li and Ah Foh were sitting
and commenced a conversation about the strike.    Five
more minutes elapsed when Ah Li and Ah Foh left the
room ostensibly to telephone to Wu Tsu-bai, but in truth
to ring up the Ford Hire Service for a car.    With the
arrival of the car, Zung, Ah Li, Ah Foh and the armed
man got into the car and left for the Ma Yue San Road.
The person who had originally accosted "Zung" near his
home did not make one of the party nor was he seen again
by the victim.

    Zung claims that he was not apprehensive as to
his safety until he was forced out of the car in Chinese
territory and that even then he did not exactly know
what was going to happen.    Questioned regarding the
persons he saw at the General Labour Union, Zung stated
that he and his escort arrived at and left the Union
offices before the usual hour for the offices to open,
thus the place was empty but for a few coolies who were
cleaning the place up ready for the day's activities.
As to the men sitting conversing in the reception room
to the east of the Meeting Hall, they were not seen by

The absence from their offices of the
General Labour Union officials may have been
pre-arranged, on the other hand the more radical
elements of the Shanghai Power Company Workers'
Strike Committee, who had plotted to murder "Zung"
may have taken advantage of the fact that at that
hour in the morning (8.30 a.m.) the place would be
almost deserted.

It is a fact that the strike was declared
on the advice of the General Labour Union and was
directed throughout by Chu Hsueh-fan (朱學範),
a leader of the Union.

The shooting of Zung Ching-loh (陳慶祿)
resulted in the Fourth District Water and Electricity
Workers' Union Strike Committee being ordered by the
General Labour Union to vacate the Reception Room in
the Foh Yeu Road premises, which had been lent as a
communication office and to some extent curbed the
activities of Chu Hsueh-fan and the strike pickets
which he more or less controlled.

Formed in December 1931 the General Labour
Union claims the allegiance of every trade union in
the Shanghai area, with the exception of the Seamen's
Union, whilst its power is enhanced by the close
co-operation of the various political and quasi-political
organs.    With such backing, the organisation in

Zung Ching-loh (陳慶祿)
Shanghai                                      D. S. I.  Golder
Sacred Heart
Hospital,             Nov.8 & 13,1933         Clerk Chiang Ching-yung
Wingkuo Road.                                 "   Kao Yen-keng
                                              (Special Branch).

    My name is Zung Ching-loh, aged 21, native
of Shanghai, residing at 17 Poh Chang Ka Loong, Nantao.
I am not married.
    I entered the services of the Shanghai Power
Company as a clerk on December 12, 1929, and have remained
with them since.    Prior to the present strike I was a
member of the Shanghai Power Company Chinese Employees' Club
(上海電力公司華人聯益社), of which Wu Tsu-bei (吳祖培)
was chairman and Fang Chien (方謙) vice-chairman.
    On October 9 or 10, I received a letter from
the Club instructing me not to go to work on pain of
punishment.    I remained at home for two days but
when I learned that practically all the clerical staff
had returned to work, I resumed.    I worked from
October 12 till the 19th without incident, although
I knew that I was being watched.
    On October 20, a little after 8 a.m. I left
my home and called a public ricksha, instructing the coolie
to take me to the Shanghai Power Company.    I had only
proceeded about 100 yards when my ricksha was stopped by
three men :-
(1) named Ah Peh (阿福) who I believe worked in the
    Riverside Power Station, aged 35 to 37, height 5' 2",
    medium build, dressed in black short jacket and
    pants, brown felt hat and black cloth shoes.    Has
    the habit of walking with his hands in the sleeves
    of his jacket.
pages.zh:
陈庆禄（Zung Ching-loh）
上海                                      副督察长 Golder
圣心
医院，             1933年11月8日及13日         职员 蒋景荣（Chiang Ching-yung，音译）
民国路。                                 "   高延庚（Kao Yen-keng，音译）
                                              （特别分部）。

    我叫陈庆禄，21岁，上海本地人，居住
在南市泊昌嘉隆17号。
    我未婚。
    我于1929年12月12日进入上海电力公司
担任职员，并一直任职至今。在本次罢工之前，
我是上海电力公司华人联益社的成员，该社由
吴祖培（Wu Tsu-bei）任主席，方谦（Fang 
Chien）任副主席。
    10月9日或10日，我收到俱乐部的一封信，
指示我不要上班，否则将受惩罚。我在家呆了
两天，但当我得知几乎所有职员都已复工时，
我便恢复了工作。从10月12日到19日，我工作
期间未发生事故，尽管我知道自己正被监视。
    10月20日上午8点刚过，我离开家，叫了一
辆公共人力车，吩咐车夫送我去上海电力公司。
我只走了大约100码，人力车就被三名男子拦
住：
(1) 名叫阿福（Ah Peh），我相信他在江边
    发电厂工作，年龄35至37岁，身高5英尺
    2英寸，中等身材，身穿黑色短夹克和裤
    子，头戴棕色毡帽，脚穿黑布鞋。有双手
    插在夹克袖子里走路的习惯。

in Riverside Power Station, aged about 35, native
of Aompo, height 5' 4", medium build, thin face,
one gold tooth in upper jaw. Was wearing blue
cotton short jacket and pants and brown cap.
(3) This man was unknown to me, but he had the appearance

The stranger (No.3) said that Wu Tsu-bei had instructed

Electricity Workers' Union Strike Committee.
Ah Fah, Ah Li and the person who was unknown to
me (No.3) and myself waited in the office for some five
minutes. The stranger then left us and entered the

此外，我相信他在江边发电厂工作，年龄约
38-39岁，身高5英尺2英寸，肤色很黑，瘦脸，
中等身材，身穿黑色长袍，头戴棕色毡帽。
那名陌生人（第3号）说，吴祖培指示他们三
人从我家把我带到位于市内佛佑路117号的总
工会办公室。我有点害怕，但认为最好还是随
他们去，于是我们步行前往工会办公室。到达
目的地后，我进入大楼的大门，穿过两个院子，
进入大办公室或会议厅（见草图）。当时办公
室里没有人，但有四五个人在东边的小房间里
说话，当时那里正被第四区水电工会罢工委员
会用作通讯办公室。
阿福（Ah Fah，原文此处拼写与前文Ah Peh/Foh不一致，依原文译）、阿李和那名我不认识的人
（第3号）以及我在办公室里等了大约五分
钟。然后陌生人离开我们，进入了

pages.en:
- 3 -
small office to the East. He closed the door and
remained inside for a few minutes and then emerged
with the person who eventually attempted to kill me.
After these two had joined us, Ah Foh and Ah Li left
and entered the office to the West (General Office on
sketch). I heard them talking but could not distinguish
the words. They returned after some five minutes
and told me that Yu Tsu Bei was waiting for us in
the offices of the th District Water & Electricity
Workers' Union, 15 Shou Ying Faung, Tien Doong Road,
Chapei. A little later Ah Foh, Ah Li, the man who
made the attempt on my life and myself all left the
General Labour Union and got into a Ford Hire car
which was waiting outside. The man in the black
long gown who originally accosted me outside my house
did not accompany us and I do not know where he went to.
During the stay at the General Labour Union
Office I did not see anyone but the men I have already
mentioned and one or two coolies who were busy cleaning
the various offices. As it was still not 9 a.m. when
we left the offices were not opened for business
and very few if any of the Union officials were on the
premises. At any rate I did not see any.
I did not pay much attention to the direction
in which the car travelled but I remember suddenly
realising that we had got out into the country near the
pages.zh:
- 3 -
东侧的一间小办公室。他关上门，在里面待了几分钟，然后和那个最终企图杀害我的人一起走了出来。在这两人加入我们要后，阿福（Ah Foh）和阿利（Ah Li）离开并进入了西侧的办公室（即草图上的总办公室）。我听见他们在谈话，但听不清具体内容。大约五分钟后他们回来，告诉我余祖培（Yu Tsu Bei）正在闸北天通庵路寿英坊15号第三区水电工人联合会的办公室里等我们。过了一会儿，阿福、阿利、那个企图谋杀我的人以及我自己都离开了总工会，坐上了一辆在外面等候的福特租赁汽车。最初在我家外面拦住我的那个穿黑色长衫的人没有随我们同行，我不知道他去了哪里。
在总工会办公室逗留期间，除了我已经提到的那些人以及一两个正在打扫各办公室的苦力外，我没有看到其他人。由于我们离开时还不到上午9点，办公室尚未开始办公，工会官员即使有人在现场也寥寥无几。无论如何，我没有看到任何官员。
我没有太注意汽车行驶的方向，但我记得突然意识到我们已经到了乡间，靠近

pages.en:
- 4 -
Ying Δiang Kiang Race Course. We were travelling along
the Ma Yueh San Road about a mile from the Race Course
when one of the men told the chauffeur to stop. We all
alighted from the car and the chauffeur was paid and moved
away. I asked why I had been brought into the country,
when Ah Foh informed me that Wu Tsu Bei would be along soon
and that we would have to wait for him. We had waited
for some five minutes when I saw an old, small, Morris
motor car approaching from the direction of the Race
Course. As the vehicle came near us it slowed down and
a man, dressed in a reddish-grey long gown of raincoat
material, jumped down, at the same time ordering the car
to proceed. Ah Foh and Ah Li greeted the man and asked
where Wu Tsu-bei had gone. The man turned round and
pointed to a house which stood in the country towards the
Race Course. Upon receiving this information we all
set out for the house, I walking in front. We
had not proceeded very far when we came to a stream
and I was on the point of turning round to ask a question
when I heard an explosion close behind me and felt a
stabbing pain in the back. I jumped forward two or
three paces and fell down. In falling I half turned
round and saw that the man who had joined us at the
General Labour Union was pointing a pistol at me. I
threw my hands up before my face and the man fired again,
one bullet striking me in the buttock and another grazed
pages.zh:
- 4 -
引翔港跑马厅。我们沿着马玉山路行驶，距离跑马厅约一英里时，其中一人让司机停车。我们都下了车，司机领了车费后驾车离去。我问为什么把我带到乡间，阿福告诉我吴祖培（Wu Tsu Bei）很快就会来，我们必须等他。我们等了大约五分钟，这时我看见一辆旧的小型莫里斯（Morris）汽车从跑马厅方向驶来。车辆靠近我们时放慢了速度，一个穿着红灰色雨衣料长衫的人跳下车，同时示意汽车继续前行。阿福和阿利向此人打招呼，并询问吴祖培去了哪里。那人转过身，指向位于跑马厅方向乡间的一所房子。得到这个消息后，我们都朝那所房子出发，我走在前面。我们没走多远就来到一条小河沟边，我正打算转身问个问题，这时听到身后不远处一声爆炸响，感到背部一阵刺痛。我向前跳了两三步，然后摔倒在地。摔倒时我半转过身，看见在总工会加入我们的那个人正用手枪指着我。我举起双手护住脸部，那人又开了一枪，一颗子弹击中我的臀部，另一颗擦过

pages.en:
- 5 -
my head. A few seconds elapsed, when the man with
the pistol came close to me and struck me three or
four times on the head with the butt of the weapon.
Immediately following this the four men ran away whilst
I being dazed remained on the ground. Some minutes
later I got up and called for help whereupon two or
three farmers working in nearby fields came to my aid.
They carried me to the road, placed me in a ricksha and
escorted me to the boundary of the Settlement from
where I was taken to Hospital.
I do not remember having seen the man
who attempted to kill me before the occasion on which
I met him at the General Labour Union, nor have I a
clear idea as to the way he was clothed.
I cannot understand why Wu Tsu Pei or
anyone should single me out as I have played no part
for or against the strike movement other than returning
to work when the majority of the clerical staff returned
on October 12 and 13.
pages.zh:
- 5 -
我的头部。过了几秒钟，持枪那人走近我，用枪托在我的头上击打了三四下。紧接着这四个人逃跑了，而我因头晕目眩仍躺在地上。几分钟后我站起来呼救，于是两三个在附近田里劳作的农民前来相助。他们把我抬到大路上，让我坐上一辆人力车，护送我到租界边界，随后我被送往医院。
我不记得在总工会见到那个企图杀害我的人之前曾见过他，我也记不清他当时的衣着细节。
我不明白为什么吴祖培（Wu Tsu Pei）或其他任何人要 singled out（ singled out 意为单独挑出/针对）我，因为除了在大多数职员于10月12日和13日复工时也返回工作岗位外，我在罢工运动中未扮演任何支持或反对的角色。

S.1, Special Branch
REPORT
Date November 7, 1933.

Subject (in full) Shanghai Power Company - Shooting of Zung Ching-loh -
Antecedents of Suspects.

Made by D. S. I. Golder Forwarded by W Ouncar

(1) Wu Tsu-Bei (吳祖培) :

A native of Soochow, was born in 1901 and
joined the Shanghai Power Company on August 8,
1921. His service was continual until October 11,
1933, when he attached himself to the ranks of
the striking employees and as a result was
dismissed from the service of the Shanghai Power
Company. He was married on October 14, 1927.
From information obtained from fellow employee's,
it would appear that "Wu" led a fairly quiet life
until about two years ago, when he began to gamble
and generally led a dissolute existence. At the
time of his dismissal from the Power Company's employ,
he was about $3,000.00 in debt, which sum was covered
chiefly by promissary notes backed by his fellow
employees.
The reason for his being connected or suspected of
complicity in the shooting of Zung Ching-loh was due
to his being mentioned in a fragmentary statement
made by "Zung" on October 20 the day on which the
attempt on his life was made. No information
or evidence has come to hand since which would
tend to dissipate or strengthen the suspicion.

(2) Tsu Ah-foh (朱阿福) :

Aged 27, native of Kiangpeh. The records
of this man cannot be traced owing to his name
having been confused with one Chu Ah-foh (朱阿福),
aged 67 who was invalided from the Power Company's
service some two months ago.

报告
日期：1933年11月7日。

主题（全称）上海电力公司 - 枪击陈庆禄（Zung Ching-loh）案 -
嫌疑人背景。

撰写人：D. S. I. Golder 转呈人：W Ouncar

(1) 吴祖培 (Wu Tsu-Bei) :

苏州人，生于1901年，于1921年8月8日加入上海电力公司。其服务一直持续至1933年10月11日，当时他加入了罢工员工的行列，因此被上海电力公司解雇。他于1927年10月14日结婚。
根据从同事处获得的信息，“吴”在大约两年前开始赌博并过着放荡的生活之前，生活相当平静。在被电力公司解雇时，他负债约3,000.00美元，这笔债务主要由其同事担保的本票覆盖。
他被牵连或涉嫌参与枪击陈庆禄（Zung Ching-loh）案的原因，是由于“陈”在10月20日（即遇袭当天）所作的一份不完整的陈述中提到了他。此后并未收到任何能够消除或加强这一嫌疑的信息或证据。

(2) 朱阿福 (Tsu Ah-foh) :

27岁，江北人。由于此人的名字与一名67岁的朱阿福（Chu Ah-foh）混淆，而后者于两个月前因病从电力公司离职，因此无法查到此人的记录。

Zung Ching-loh (陳慶祿) during the
statement previously mentioned referred to an "Ah Foh"
as one of the persons concerned with the shooting but
did not state that he was one of the men who actually
did the shooting.
(3) Ah Li (阿利)
The only man of this name "(Lieu) Ah Li"
(劉阿利) has been with the Power Company for about
3 years. He has not been prominent in the present
strike and may be perfectly innocent of the crime
in question.
Zung Ching loh mentioned Ah Li's name on
October 20, but failed to explain the exact connection.
It is generally believed that he had proclaimed
himself to be a staunch supporter of the strikers whilst
at the same time he was passing information regarding
their activities on to the management.
It is learned that Zung Ching-loh has sufficiently
recovered to be questioned; a statement will therefore
be obtained from him during the next few days.

                                D. S. I.

7584

PAID ASSASSINS
OF STRIKERS
An Outrage Described
by Victim

"They took me to the General
Labour Union, where the assassin
who attempted to murder me
boarded the motorcar, which drove
to a spot near Yinghsiangkong,"
said Zung Ching-loh, yesterday,
when sufficiently recovered from
the attempt made on his life three
weeks ago by strikers of the Shang-
hai Power Company.
Zung, a clerk in the employ of
the company, at all times refused
to leave his post. After firing a
number of shots, two of which
entered his body, one near the
heart, his assailants boarded their
vehicle again and left him in the
fields to die. He was picked up
some time later and, although his
life was despaired of, he is now
convalescing in hospital.
According to Zung, he left his
house in Nantao on the fatal morn-
ing and had gone about 100 yards,
when three men accosted him, say-
ing that he was wanted at the
union office. There, four men
were waiting. After a short con-
versation, a car was brought. The
original party, reinforced by one
man from the scene of the assault,
drove to the union office, then
"I do not believe that he was a
striker," added Zung, "he was of
the bandit type, although at that
time I did not suspect why he
joined us."

《字林西报》，1933年11月9日，星期四
7584

罢工者的
职业杀手
受害者描述暴行

“他们把我带到总工会，那个企图谋杀我的刺客在那里上了汽车，车子开到了引翔港附近的一个地方，”陈庆禄昨天说。此时距三周前上海电力公司罢工者对他进行的谋杀未遂事件发生已有段时间，他的身体已足够恢复。
陈是该公司的职员，始终拒绝离开岗位。袭击者向他开了数枪，其中两枪击中他的身体，一枪靠近心脏，随后袭击者重新上车，将他留在田野中等死。一段时间后他被发现，虽然当时对他的生还已不抱希望，但他现在正在医院休养康复。
据陈称，案发当天早上他离开南市的家，走了约100码时，有三个人拦住他，说工会办公室找他。在那里，有四个人在等候。简短交谈后，叫来了一辆汽车。最初的几人加上袭击现场加入的一人，乘车前往工会办公室，然后
“我不相信他是罢工者，”陈补充道，“他是那种匪徒类型的人，尽管当时我并没有怀疑他为什么要加入我们。”

REGISTRY
5210
Yangtszepoo Station,
Date Nov. 2nd. 19 33.

REPORT

Subject (in full) Further to attempted murder of an employee of the
Shanghai Power Company named Zung Ching Loh.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Willgoss

Sir,

Since the last report was forwarded C.D.S.s 87 and 62 (.)
14 and 11 (Y.R.) and detectives attached to Yangtszepoo Station
have made diligent enquiries in the Settlement, French Concession,
Nantao and Chapei but have learned every little regarding the
whereabouts of the wanted men.

There is a persistant rumour that the three men are hiding at
the General Labour Union's premises at 117 Foh Yue Road, City,
but it can not be confirmed.

It has been ascertained that the full name of the suspect
referred to in the initial report as Ah Li is Lieu Ah Li.

Information has been received that he has escaped to Ningpo
and may return in two or three weeks.

A circular order of arrest for Wu Tsau Bei, and Tsu Ah Foh,
has been received and is on file at Yangtszepoo Station.

Reward notice No. 1176 offering $5,000.00 for information
leading to the arrest and conviction of the persons responsible
for this crime has been issued and given wide publicity.

The Complainant is making very favourable progress and will
undoubtedly recover.

I am, Sir,

Your obedient servant,
Willgoss

报告

主题（全称） 继上海电力公司员工陈庆禄（Zung Ching Loh）遇刺未遂案之后。

撰写及转呈人：副督察 Willgoss

先生，

自上次报告转呈以来，刑事侦缉处警员 87号和 62号 (.)
14号和 11号 (洋泾浜) 以及附属杨树浦分局的侦探在租界、法租界、
南市和闸北进行了勤勉的调查，但关于通缉犯的下落几乎一无所获。

一直有谣言称这三个人藏在市内福州路117号总工会的 premises（处所/房产），
但无法证实。

经查实，初步报告中被称为阿利的嫌疑人的全名是刘阿利（Lieu Ah Li）。

收到消息称他已逃往宁波，可能在两到三周内返回。

已收到对吴祖培（Wu Tsau Bei）和朱阿福（Tsu Ah Foh）的逮捕通缉令，
并已存档于杨树浦分局。

悬赏通告第1176号已发布并广泛宣传，提供5,000.00美元奖金，
以征集导致逮捕和定罪对此罪行负责人员的信息。

原告恢复情况非常顺利，无疑将会康复。

我是，先生，
